claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a statistically homogeneous elemental distribution at its surface.
Controlled electrochemical potential cycling induces selective surface segregation in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os are more oxophilic than Pt and Pd in this catalyst.
Potential cycling oxidizes Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os.
Oxidized Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os preferentially migrate from the surface into the particle bulk.
Potential cycling consequently enriches the catalyst surface in Pt and Pd.
A Pt/Pd-enriched surface improves the adsorption geometry of ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
The Pt/Pd-enriched surface lowers activation barriers for ethanol oxidation.
The Pt/Pd-enriched surface minimizes poisoning during ethanol oxidation.
Potential-cycled catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current than untreated catalysts.
Potential-cycled catalysts will show greater selectivity toward acetaldehyde rather than complete oxidation products.
Potential-cycled catalysts will have enhanced durability, manifested as slower activity decline, relative to untreated catalysts.
The proposed intervention is potential cycling from 0.0 to 1.0 V versus RHE for approximately 50 cycles.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to catalyst particles smaller than approximately 10 nm.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to ethanol oxidation in acidic media at ambient temperature.
Potential cycling must avoid irreversible over-oxidation or dissolution for the proposed beneficial effect to hold.
